draft.title: Improving crop yields
card: Crop yield is the amount of useful plant material grown on an area of land. Yield depends partly on how efficiently a crop photosynthesises.
CRISPR-Cas9 is a gene-editing tool. It uses a guide RNA to lead the Cas9 enzyme to a chosen DNA sequence, where it cuts the DNA so the gene can be changed.
Rubisco is a target for editing. It is slow and also reacts with oxygen, which wastes energy. An improved Rubisco could fix carbon more efficiently.
Scientists could edit crop genes this way to raise photosynthesis and so raise yields. Much of this work is still being researched and tested.
draft.remember: CRISPR-Cas9 could edit genes such as Rubisco to make photosynthesis more efficient and raise yields.

a.q: What is the role of the guide RNA in CRISPR-Cas9 editing of a crop?
opts: It leads Cas9 to the chosen DNA sequence
It cuts the DNA at the chosen sequence
It carries the new Rubisco protein into cells
It makes the plant take in more light
a.why: The guide RNA matches the target sequence and leads the Cas9 enzyme to it. Cas9 is the enzyme that cuts the DNA, so cutting is not the guide's job.
a.clue: The guide RNA works like an address.

b.q: A research team wants a wheat crop to photosynthesise more efficiently using CRISPR-Cas9. Which target fits the aim best?
opts: The gene for a Rubisco that wastes less energy
The gene for a protein that stores wheat grain
The gene for an enzyme that digests starch in flour
The gene for a pigment that colours the grain
b.why: Rubisco takes part in carbon fixation and also reacts wastefully with oxygen. Improving it could raise photosynthesis and yield. The other genes act in grain storage, digestion or colour, not in photosynthetic efficiency.
b.clue: Which enzyme fixes carbon in the Calvin cycle?

a.best: It leads Cas9 to the chosen DNA sequence

b.best: The gene for a Rubisco that wastes less energy

problems.detail: "Edit genes such as Rubisco" calls Rubisco a gene. Rubisco is an enzyme (a protein). The line should say "genes such as those coding for Rubisco" so students do not mix up genes and proteins.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer that matches the card, and the explanations agree with it. The only problem is that the remember line calls Rubisco a gene when it is an enzyme coded for by genes.
